subject: Embeddings & Reranker MAP — load validation, SLO targets, and close cadence
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@atlasfind.com>, Priya Rao <priya@atlasfind.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Embeddings & Reranker MAP — initial scope and validation plan

Sam / Priya — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a lightweight MAP (sheet tab: "Load + Perf") outlining the evaluation milestones you asked for: latency/throughput baselines, concurrency boundaries, and a go/no-go criteria recommended by our solutions and SRE teams.

High-level asks from AtlasFind:
- Verify embeddings throughput at your expected batch sizes and query patterns (mostly short search queries, mean length ~18 tokens).
- Validate reranker p95 latency under candidate set sizes of 10/50.
- Demonstrate stable tail behavior during 30-minute sustained load + 5x spike.

Quick notes on what's in the MAP:
- Week 1: Baseline functional eval (sanity) + configuration (model variants, quantization profile).
- Week 2: Load validation with synthetic traffic and a replay of 10k real queries (we'll provide anonymized sample).
- Week 3: Final run and executive summary + handoff doc.

Please confirm: target close window you mentioned was "end of month" (Feb 28). If so, we need the load validation run completed by Tue 23rd to leave time for contract review.

Attachments: MAP-AtlasFind-v1.xlsx (MAP + test plan)

Next step: Marissa will coordinate the replay dataset and runbook.

—Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sam Carter <sam.carter@atlasfind.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Embeddings & Reranker MAP — initial scope and validation plan

Thanks Jordan — looping in SRE and Applied ML.

Sam / Priya, quick notes on the test topology we'll run unless you request changes:
- Embeddings endpoint: model=redwood-embed-4-small (vector dim=1536). Tests: steady-state QPS levels of 200, 500, 1k with batch sizes 1/8/32. Measure p50/p95/p99 and vector return time.
- Reranker endpoint: model=redwood-rerank-2 (pairwise logits). Candidate set sizes: 10 and 50. Concurrency ramps: 10 -> 50 -> 100. We'll capture TTFT (time-to-first-token where applicable), end-to-end latency, and memory/GPU metrics.
- Test harness: k6 for steady throughput profiles + a smaller Locust suite for the sampled replay.

Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Embeddings: p95 <= 90ms at target QPS (500) and batch size 8.
- Reranker: p95 <= 400ms for candidate=10 at 50 concurrent workers. If candidate=50, p95 <= 700ms.
- No unexpected OOMs or server restarts during 30-minute sustained run.

I'll schedule the replay ingestion and share the replay dataset and runbook by EOD tomorrow. If you want us to use a different model variant or quantization profile, call it out now.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Priya Rao <priya@atlasfind.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Carter <sam.carter@atlasfind.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Embeddings & Reranker MAP — initial scope and validation plan

Thanks — that plan looks good. Two clarifications from our side:
1) Replay dataset: we'll provide 10k anonymized queries in the same CSV format as last time; can you confirm you will preserve ordering for the spike tests?
2) Contract cadence: we can push contract review onto the 24th (internal legal OK) — would you still expect a final perf report before the 24th so we can sign by 28th?

Also curious about cost implications — if you run with quantized embeddings (int8), what delta in latency/throughput should we expect versus FP16? Not blocking the run but want the numbers in the report.

—Priya
Head of Search | AtlasFind
priya@atlasfind.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@atlasfind.com>, Sam Carter <sam.carter@atlasfind.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Feb 2027 14:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Embeddings & Reranker MAP — load runs complete (initial results)

Quick update — we executed the planned runs this morning (attached raw data + graphs). Summary highlights below. Full CSV + traces attached (load-results-20270223.csv, k6-embeddings-graphs-20270223.png, reranker-latency-traces-20270223.json).

Embedding endpoint (redwood-embed-4-small, vector dim=1536) — replay + synthetic mix:
- Test config: 30-minute steady window at 500 QPS, batch sizes 8; spike test: 5 minute 5x burst to 2.5k QPS.
- p50 latency: 14 ms; p95: 48 ms; p99: 120 ms.
- Sustained throughput: stable at 500 QPS with ~3% variance. No restarts.
- Int8 quantization run: p95 improved ~10% (to ~43 ms) and inferred end-to-end cost reduction ~12% at this load.

Reranker endpoint (redwood-rerank-2) — pairwise reranker with candidate sets:
- Candidate=10, concurrency ramp to 50 workers:
  - p50: 98 ms; p95: 305 ms; p99: 520 ms.
- Candidate=50, concurrency ramp to 100 workers:
  - p50: 360 ms; p95: 710 ms; p99: 1.2s.
- Observed GPU mem pressure at candidate=50, sustained high concurrency — we saw sustained allocator churn and a small (single-digit) increase in tail latency during the 5x spike. No OOMs.

Operational notes:
- TTL cache/batching parameters used (batch size 8 for embeddings) — see runbook tab in the MAP for exact env vars.
- We captured TTFT for reranker (~60–80ms p50) which accounts for model setup and tokenization steps; we included trace markers in the JSON attachment.

Recommendation and next steps:
- For production: use int8 embeddings with the same batch profile for cost/latency sweet spot.
- For reranker at large candidate sets (50+), consider sharding candidates across two concurrent reranker instances or pre-filtering to a smaller candidate set.
- If AtlasFind needs a hard p95 <= 400ms for candidate=50, we recommend a Dedicated pool with slightly larger GPU profiles (estimate +25% infra).

Ask: Sam/Priya — can you confirm these numbers meet your acceptance criteria? If yes, Jordan, can we push to legal for signature on 24th as planned?

—Marissa

From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@atlasfind.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@atlasfind.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Embeddings & Reranker MAP — load runs complete (initial results)

This looks good — really helpful and clear. The embedding p95 is well within our expectations. For reranker: candidate=10 numbers are fine; for candidate=50 we'll take the recommendation to shard or pre-filter (we'll prototype a 2-stage filter).

We confirm: please proceed with the contract push on the 24th. Legal will aim to turn around by the 28th. Also, please include the int8 vs FP16 cost delta in the final one-pager — Priya wants that called out.

Thanks everyone — solid work.

—Sam
